Hoar
HOR
adj. (white or grey with age or frost)
Old English har, grey, venerable. The Authorized Version uses it of the frost on the wilderness ground the morning the manna came, and of the grey head of an old man.

Biblical Definition

Two pictures share one word. The first is the morning of the manna: when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground. The bread of heaven arrived looking like frost, and had to be gathered every morning, and bred worms if hoarded. The second is age. David charges Solomon concerning Joab, let not his hoar head go down to the grave in peace, and concerning Shimei, his hoar head bring thou down to the grave with blood — grey hair is no immunity from justice. Yet the same greyness is honoured where it is honourable: the hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness, which is a conditional crown and says so. The verse the dictionary keeps above all is Isaiah's, where God takes the hoar head to himself: and even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you. The God who made a man in the womb undertakes to carry him out of the world.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): white; grey with age; white with frost; hence, venerable, applied to age.

expand to see more

HOAR, a. White; as hoar frost; hoary.

HOAR, a. White or grey with age; as hoar hairs.

HOARY, a. White or whitish; white or grey with age; hence, venerable.

FROST, n. A fluid congealed by cold; also, the white particles of dew congealed on the ground.

AGE, n. The whole duration of a being, whether animal or vegetable; a period of life.

Key Scripture

Isa 46:4 — "And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you."

Exo 16:14 — "And when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground."

Pro 16:31 — "The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness."

1Ki 2:6 — "Do therefore according to thy wisdom, and let not his hoar head go down to the grave in peace."

Modern Corruption

Age is treated as decline to be delayed and hidden, and the old as a class to be managed; Scripture makes grey hair an honour where righteousness earned it, refuses it as a shelter from justice, and makes God himself the one who carries a man to the end.

expand to see more

A culture organised around youth has two settled opinions about old age, that it is a medical problem and that it is an embarrassment, and Isaiah 46:4 contradicts both. The verse is God speaking against the idols of Babylon, which have to be carried on beasts and are a burden to the weary. God's claim is the opposite: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you. The idol is freight; the LORD is the porter. And the span he commits to is the whole of it, from the belly to hoar hairs, which is the strongest statement in the Old Testament of preserving grace over a lifetime.

Proverbs supplies the balance so that the honour due to age is not sentimental. The hoary head is a crown of glory — if it be found in the way of righteousness. And David's charge about Joab shows the other edge: a long life of bloodshed does not buy a peaceful grave. The dictionary therefore honours the aged as the fifth commandment requires, refuses the flattery that treats years alone as wisdom, and holds out the promise to those growing old in Christ that the carrying is God's work and not theirs.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew kephowr (H3713), hoar frost; seybah (H7872), grey hair, old age; cabal (H5445), to bear a load.

expand to see more

Hebrew kephowr (H3713) — hoar frost; as small as the hoar frost on the ground.

Hebrew seybah (H7872) — grey hair, and so old age; his hoar head, and to hoar hairs.

Hebrew cabal (H5445) — to bear a burden, to carry; I will bear; even I will carry.

Hebrew 'ateret (H5850) — a crown, a diadem; the hoary head is a crown of glory.

Hebrew malat (H4422) — to slip away, to deliver, to rescue; and will deliver you.

Usage

"“as small as the hoar frost on the ground” — the morning the manna came."

"“even to hoar hairs will I carry you” — God's undertaking for old age."

"“let not his hoar head go down to the grave in peace” — grey hair as no shelter from justice."
